content:
[Goal]

- Is there a need to specify both "friends" and "circle of friends" in this case? You also refer to each group of students as a "friend group" in the Input section. Wondering if this can be standardised to avoid confusion.

- "insert himself into the last position of his circle of friends who are already queueing" - perhaps a clearer phrasing might be "insert himself right behind the last friend in the queue"? To further specify what "last" means, you could add that the last friend refers to the friend closest to the tail end of the queue.

[Input]

- For your consideration: would it be helpful to add an additional line of input right before the events line to indicate the total number of events? This might aid parsing for some languages. Not sure if this was intended since the friend groups are given in the same manner.

[Constraints]

- Please state that there will be at least one dequeueing event.

- Please state that the order of events are valid with respect to the student(s) involved (e.g. that a student will never rejoin the queue whilst simultaneously still being in the queue, that there will never be a dequeueing event with no students in the queue, etc.)

- (optional) This is implied, but you could state that each student has a unique ID number.

[Cases]

- Consider adding a case where there are a large number of lone wolves and where the queue grows very large.

- Consider adding some cases where there are a large number of students (~500-1000) to handle.

- Consider adding a case as follows: where A and B are friends, and the queue is (head) A R1 R2 R3 ... RN (tail) (where R are random students). Then have B join the queue, A leave the queue, A rejoin the queue, B leave the queue, B rejoin the queue, etc.

Thank you!

Haha, @User123 posted their comment literally a minute before I tried to post mine. I've since edited my comment a bit so I wouldn't just repeat their great suggestions.

Goal
* Please remove "or circle of friends", as it suggests that friendships may extend beyond the immediate friend groups.

Input
* (Optional) Consider extending the input to include:
  (a) the number of students in each friend group (similar to the format used in your other puzzle "Bin packing"), and
  (b) the number of events.

Constraints
* Please specify the range for the number of students in each friend group.

Cases
* Please remove all trailing newlines from input.

* Please remove all trailing newlines from output.

* Is the following scenario currently covered: a student rejoins the queue before the rest of their friend group has fully dequeued? If not, please add a corresponding case pair.

Thanks.

Thanks for the many suggestions. They are now largely implemented. Together with @User123 's comments, the statements, input data structure, the validating solution and also test cases are updated. The trailing newline problem is fixed.
Will review it again later for further improvements.
A cycling friend group is made in "Rejoining the Queue" test case. Interesting suggestion from @User123.

Goal
* Second paragraph: Please change "were found... would jump... were found... would join" to "is found... will jump... is found... will join".

Input
* Line 1: Please add "Two space-separated" before "integers".

Constraints
* Please change "the same person cannot queue at two locations simultaneously" to "a student will not enqueue again before dequeueing" for clarity and simplicity.

Constraints / Cases
* Long queue (Test/Validator 8) violates the ID constraint.

Stub generator
* Please change Line 3 to `loopline e event:int`.

Cases
* I'm wondering whether the scenario mentioned in my previous message is already covered. It's essentially an extended version of @User123's cycling friend group idea, except that the enqueueing/dequeueing order doesn't necessarily follow a neat repeating cycle. For example (1, 2, 3, 4, 5 belong to the same friend group):

1
2
3
1
4
5
3
1
5
3
2
4

If covered, please let me know which case pair covers this scenario.

Thanks.

The above points are now fixed. About rejoining Cases,
"Rejoining the Queue" has a close-loop pattern 1 2 1 2 1... (IDs 3057, 3096)
"Rejoining the Queue Validator" has a pattern involving three items: 1 2 3 1 2 3 2 1 ... (IDs 3558, 3054, 3010)
Is it satisfactory?

Thanks for pointing these out. I did notice the cyclic patterns you mentioned.

My earlier comment was mainly about whether there's coverage for a less structured rejoining pattern.

Since only the tests are visible to players while the validators are hidden, players can currently observe only the neat cyclic pattern, but not the slightly disrupted variant.

A wholly non-cyclic rejoining pattern presents a more generalised scenario for broader stress coverage. I would appreciate it if you could consider either modifying an existing case pair or adding another pair to incorporate such a pattern.
Just to clarify, not replacing @User123's cyclic pattern, but having both patterns.
